1221.quote_or_event: “This dream like happening did not let me meet my beloved. Now the death-like night of separation neither ends nor terminates.”
1221.explanation: Bhai Gurdas laments that the meeting with his Beloved slipped away, leaving a night of separation that feels like death and will not end.
1221.tie_back: The Kural's wife tells the evening it is no gentle dusk but a killing time for wives whose husbands are away; Bhai Gurdas likewise feels the night of separation as death itself.
1221.source: Bhai Gurdas, Kabit Savaiye, Kabit 219 (English translation as given on BaniDB)
1221._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB; strong fit on the nightfall of separation as deadly, but Bhai Gurdas's Kabits are early exegesis, not scripture, his time-word is night rather than dusk, and the love is for the Guru, spiritual rather than romantic.

1222.quote_or_event: “The chakvi bird does not long for sleepy eyes; without her beloved, she does not sleep.”
1222.explanation: Guru Nanak points to the chakvi, the bird said to be parted from her mate every night, as an image of the soul that cannot rest without its Lord.
1222.tie_back: The Kural's wife sees the dim dusk as a fellow sufferer and asks whether its partner is as hard-hearted as hers; Guru Nanak too finds in nature, in the chakvi parted from her mate at nightfall, a companion in the pain of separation.
1222.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1273, Raag Malaar, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1222._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa); reasonable fit on a creature of the night who shares the lover's separation, but the Kural addresses the evening itself, not a bird, and Guru Nanak's longing is spiritual, not romantic.

1223.quote_or_event: “In the month of Poh, the cold does not touch those, whom the Husband Lord hugs close in His Embrace.”
1223.explanation: In his Barah Maha (song of the twelve months), Guru Arjan says the frost of the winter month cannot touch the bride whom her Lord holds close.
1223.tie_back: The Kural's pale evening arrives beaded with dew, and the wife's sorrow buds with it; Guru Arjan implies the converse, that cold and frost wound only the bride whose Husband is away.
1223.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 135, Raag Maajh, Barah Maha, Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1223._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa); next-best match: both tie cold, dewy weather to the lot of the separated bride, but the Guru states it from the side of union, and his love is spiritual, not romantic.

1224.quote_or_event: “Fareed, that body, within which love of the Lord does not well up - look upon that body as a cremation ground.”
1224.explanation: Sheikh Farid uses the grim image of the cremation ground for a body untouched by the longing of separation from God.
1224.tie_back: The Kural's wife feels the evening come at her like enemies onto a field of slaughter; Farid also reaches for a place of the dead, though he applies it to the heart that feels no longing at all.
1224.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1379, Saloks of Sheikh Farid (salok 36) (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1224._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa); next-best match: both use a place of death in the setting of separation, but Farid's cremation ground is the loveless body, the reverse of the Kural's grieving wife, and his love is spiritual.

1225.quote_or_event: “When the sun rises, she sees her beloved with her eyes; she bows and touches his feet.”
1225.explanation: Guru Nanak completes the image of the chakvi: parted from her mate all night, she is reunited with him when the sun comes up.
1225.tie_back: The Kural's wife asks what kindness she did the morning that it treats her gently, and what wrong she did the evening that it torments her; the chakvi's lot shows the same pattern, with nightfall bringing separation and sunrise bringing reunion.
1225.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1273, Raag Malaar, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1225._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa); strong fit on morning as the friend and night as the foe of the separated lover, though Guru Nanak draws a lesson about the soul's devotion rather than blaming the hours, and the love is spiritual.

1226.quote_or_event: “If my Husband Lord comes to my home, then I obtain everything.”
1226.explanation: Guru Arjan's bride-soul says that the Lord's presence in her home is all she needs; everything else follows from it.
1226.tie_back: The Kural's wife never knew evening could hurt until her husband left; the Guru's bride likewise finds that with the Husband at home nothing is lacking, so pain enters only with his absence.
1226.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1361, Phunhay, Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1226._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa); next-best match: it shares the idea that the beloved's presence keeps every sorrow away, but it has no before-and-after discovery of the evening's pain, and the love is spiritual, not romantic.

1227.quote_or_event: “Many talk of the pain and suffering of separation; O pain, you are the ruler of all.”
1227.explanation: Sheikh Farid crowns the pain of separation (birha) as a sovereign whose rule nothing escapes.
1227.tie_back: The Kural traces love-sickness budding in the morning and blooming fully by evening; Farid too sees the pain of separation grow until it rules over everything.
1227.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1379, Saloks of Sheikh Farid (salok 36) (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1227._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa); next-best match: it shares the overwhelming power of separation's pain, but has nothing of the Kural's bud-to-bloom image, and Farid praises this longing for God as precious, a spiritual not romantic love.

1228.quote_or_event: “Blessed, blessed is that flute which the Lord plays.”
1228.explanation: Bhagat Namdev celebrates the flute of the Lord, the pastoral image of Krishna, as the sound of divine sweetness.
1228.tie_back: In the Kural the herdsman's flute at dusk heralds the burning evening and wounds the lonely wife; in Namdev the cowherd's flute is a blessing, so the two use the same instrument with opposite feeling.
1228.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 988, Raag Maalee Gauraa, Bhagat Namdev (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1228._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa); weak, next-best match by contrast: both have the pastoral flute, but Namdev's flute brings joy where the Kural's brings pain, and Sikh teaching reads it as the divine sound, not a Krishna love scene.

1229.quote_or_event: “Fareed, I thought that I was in trouble; the whole world is in trouble!”
1229.explanation: Sheikh Farid discovers that the suffering he thought was his alone is shared by everyone around him.
1229.tie_back: The Kural's wife feels that as evening spreads, the whole town is bewildered and grieving just as she is; Farid likewise looks out and finds his own pain mirrored in all the world.
1229.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1382, Saloks of Sheikh Farid (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1229._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa); near one-to-one on private grief seen in everyone else, though Farid's trouble is the general suffering of worldly life rather than a wife's evening loneliness.

1230.quote_or_event: “Kabeer, the snake of separation from the Lord abides within my mind; it does not respond to any mantra. One who is separated from the Lord does not live; if he does live, he goes insane.”
1230.explanation: Kabir describes separation from God as a snakebite no charm can cure, one that either kills or drives the sufferer mad.
1230.tie_back: The Kural's wife says the life that has held on until now is dying this evening as she thinks of her husband gone after wealth; Kabir likewise says that one parted from the beloved cannot go on living.
1230.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1368, Saloks of Bhagat Kabir (salok 76) (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
1230._accuracy_note: Verified verbatim via BaniDB (Sant Singh Khalsa); reasonable fit on separation as mortal, but Kabir says nothing of a husband drawn away by wealth, and his separation is from God, a spiritual not romantic love.
